Good morning, Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and Distinguished Members of the
Joint Standing Committee on Legal and Veterans Affairs:
I am Senator Brad Farrin; and I represent the people of Senate District 3, which includes several communities in Kennebec, Penobscot and Somerset Counties. I am here today to talk about a promise. It's the promise we make as a state to support those who serve our nation and, just as importantly, the families who stand with them. LD 2130 is about keeping that promise.
Right now, living within our communities is an incredible, untapped reservoir of talent: our
military spouses. These are individuals who are educated, resilient, and ready to work; yet they face a staggering 21% unemployment rate. Why? Because their commitment to their family's service means they are uprooted every two to three years. Their careers are put on hold, not for
lack of skill but for lack of stability.
This isn't just a challenge for these families; it's a missed opportunity for Maine. In a time when employers are actively seeking skilled, dedicated talent, we have a motivated workforce right in our backyard that we could help integrate.
LD 2130 presents a simple, powerful, and commonsense solution. It provides a framework for
employers to give hiring preference to military spouses. This is not a mandate but an opporttuiity and a tool to help Maine employers connect with an exceptional talent pool.
Think of it as a win-win. We help military families achieve the financial stability they deserve
which, in turn, strengthens the readiness of our service members; and we give the State of Maine
a competitive edge in recruiting dedicated, skilled, and adaptable professionals.
You will also be receiving written testimony from our partners at the Defense-State Liaison Office. In that testimony you will be provided a more-detailed look at the data and the day-to-
day realities our military families face. My purpose today is to frame the issue for what it is: a
chance for Maine to lead and a chance to align our economic needs with our values. So far eight states have enacted legislation providing military spouses with employment preference in state or
private employment, our neighbors to the west in New Hampshire being one.

Sponsored by Sen. Bradlee Farrin Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs

Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee Veterans and
Legal Affairs: I am Margaret Eddy, Policy Analyst for the State of Maine Bureau of Human Resources. l am providing testimony today in support of LD 2130, An Act to Support Employment Opportunities for
Military Spouses.
This is a bill that is easy for the State of Maine Bureau of Human Resources to get behind. The State of
Maine already provides a hiring preference which guarantees an inten/iew to veterans and gold star
spouses who meet the minimum qualification of the position; providing them a foot in the door and
opportunity to distinguish themselves. This legislation would merely extend that preference to the
spouses of active-duty members of the United States Armed Forces, Reserves, and National Guard.
Much is demanded from the spouses of our military men and women; often this means uprooting themselves when their partner is restationed, disrupting their own employment and making building their own career challenging. In addition, during deployments they may be temporarily parenting alone and
shouldering household duty by themselves.
The State is Maine's 2"" largest employer and state jobs are highly sought after for their quality of workplace, benefits, and opportunity to sen/e. Across our many departments and agencies, the State offers fulfilling careers in a broad array of professions. Whether you're an attorney, accountant, biologist, equipment operator, nurse, social worker, engineer, human resources professional, information technology expert, law enforcement officer, social worker, or transportation worker, the State has job opportunities for you. In addition, working for the State of Maine can often provide stability, regular hours, and flexibility that a military spouse who is temporarily parenting alone while their spouse is deployed
needs. This bill recognizes the excellent fit that the State and military spouses may be.
ln conclusion, we encourage the Committee to vote LD 2130 Ought to Pass.

Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Veterans and Legal Affairs, my name is Melinda Kinney, and I am here today on behalf of Martin's Point Health Care in support of LD2l 30, An Act to Support Employment Opportunities for Military Spouses.
Martin's Point Health Care is a not-for-profit organization sewing our community's health care needs with the highest-quality care and coverage. As an organization providing both direct health care services and health
insurance plans, we are uniquely positioned to fulfill our mission to create a healthier community through
authentic relationships built on trust. Martin's Point offers a military health plan under the Uniformed Services
Family Health Plan (USFHP) to over 46,000 beneficiaries in six states - Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, upstate New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. USFHP is a TRICARE Prime program delivering health benefits to active -
duty family members and retired military veterans. Martin's Point also offers Medicare Advantage plans and has
six health primary care centers in Maine and New Hampshire.
In Maine, Martin's Point covers over 15,000 lives through USFHP and we work firsthand with active-duty family
members including the spouses that are the focus of LD21 30. Supporting our military members and their families is at the heart of our mission at Martin's Point. Economic stability plays a key role in providing families with the
essential items needed to stay healthy and to strengthen family readiness. Active-duty spouses face several
significant employment challenges due to frequent relocations; each move often means starting over professionally which often includes building new networks and navigating completely different dynamics. There
are frequently geographic limitations since military installations are often in areas with limited job markets or
there is an employer reluctance to hire military spouses due to the shorter-term length of employment. In some cases, there are employment gaps and resume concerns that arise from frequent relocations. These are just a few examples active-duty spouses face in the employment arena which can unfairly dismiss their qualifications and talent. By giving a qualified candidate, the opportunity to meet with the hiring employer, it helps eliminate one
more barrier and/or bias that may overshadow the candidate's talent and skill set.
Please support LD2l 30, thank you.
